gen-gf-sniglet-fs-supreme: Supreme reads as a thick, heavy-looking band of text, its letters held open rather than curled shut, which gives it real presence. Sniglet matches that with a monoline stroke from start to finish.
gen-gf-sniglet-general-sans: Sniglet brings a distinctive display voice, its terminals stopping short of curling back in and its stroke staying level. And General Sans does the quieter work, with an x-height that fills the line and smooth curves.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-orbit: Rounded and slightly floaty, Sniglet's heading letters stop short of curling back in. And Orbit follows with sans-serif characters that sit apart from one another, each stroke the same rope-like thickness, so the two feel like close cousins.
gen-gf-sniglet-manrope: Sniglet's terminals stop short instead of curling back in. Manrope has a bright open gap at every curved letter's mouth and a modest step from capital to lowercase, which gives the heading a friendly partner.
gen-gf-sniglet-satoshi: Distinctive is the mood Sniglet sets, its terminals halting before they curl and its lowercase sitting moderate in height. Satoshi takes the lead for reading, with a soaring x-height and a wide-open e that never looks squeezed.
gen-gf-sniglet-switzer: Commanding, though quiet in rhythm, Sniglet lets its terminals stop short of curling back in. Switzer does the reading work, with tubular, wire-like letterforms and a tall waist line that keep lines easy to follow.
gen-gf-sniglet-work-sans: Sniglet has a distinctive display look, its terminals stopping short of curling back in. Work Sans then carries a longer read in a modern sans, with a high mean line and joins as thick as its strokes.
gen-gf-snowburst-one-fs-bespoke-sans: Snowburst One is cut like a stencil sheet, with wide bridges between letters and tall lowercase. But Bespoke Sans reads sharp and refined, leaving generous space between curve ends and the stem across a longer passage.
gen-gf-snowburst-one-gf-abeezee: Stenciled, bold and tall, Snowburst One has wide bridges between its letters and an opening like a sprung paper clip. And ABeeZee reads smoothly after it, its terminals finishing well clear of the stem in a longer passage.
gen-gf-snowburst-one-gf-aldrich: Stencil cuts, wide bridges, tall lowercase: Snowburst One announces itself at once. Aldrich does the opposite job, tracing one thick thread with cupped round letters and an x-height close to the cap height.
